hook: A rifle kicks back when it fires, a skater drifts backward after throwing a ball, and two pool balls share their motion when they collide. All three follow one rule: with no net external push, a system cannot change its total momentum. Choosing the system decides when the rule applies.

prereq.q: Newton's third law says the force A exerts on B is
options: equal in size and opposite to the force B exerts on A
in the same direction as B on A
prereq.why: Third-law pairs are equal and opposite.

prereq.q: The velocity of a system's center of mass is

figure.caption: For cart A alone, B's push is external and A's momentum changes; for both carts, the pushes are internal and the total momentum stays constant.

chain.cause: Two objects in a system push on each other
chain.effect: the third law makes the forces, and their impulses, equal and opposite

chain.cause: The internal impulses are equal and opposite
chain.effect: one object's momentum gain is the other's loss, so internal forces cannot change the total

chain.cause: The net external force on the system is zero
chain.effect: the system's total momentum, and its center of mass's velocity, stay constant

chain.cause: An object is left out of the system
chain.effect: its forces become external and the system's momentum can change

ideas: Internal forces come in third-law pairs, so their impulses cancel: they move momentum between parts but never change the total.
Conservation of momentum: when the net external force on a system is zero, its total momentum is constant: Σp_before = Σp_after.
The choice of system decides whether momentum is constant. A cart alone in a collision is not; both carts together are.
With no net external force, the center of mass moves at constant velocity, whatever the parts do.
Justify with the condition: "the net external force on the two-cart system is zero", never "because momentum is conserved".

misconception.wrong: Momentum is constant because of conservation of momentum.
misconception.right: Momentum is constant for a system on which the net external force is zero. Name the system and say why the external forces add to zero (they balance, or are negligible during a brief collision).

summary: Internal forces cancel in pairs, so only external forces change a system's momentum. With zero net external force, total momentum and the center of mass's velocity stay constant. Choosing the system decides which forces are external; always state the condition.
